clue.text: Perhaps buy it in old money for convenience

parts.note: EX- is a prefix for former or old

indicators.note: the dying is put inside the coins, so this word signals a container

parts.note: pence are small British coins
to buy it is slang for to perish, one example of meeting your end

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that paying in pre-decimal coinage might be the handy option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old money' looks like one phrase meaning pre-decimal coinage, but 'old' and 'money' give separate pieces, with 'in' setting the death inside the coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedience is doing what is practical or advantageous, a synonym for convenience.

clue.text: Ancient character in The Thunderer

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the newspaper's nickname, so this word signals a hidden run

explanation.surface: An old figure appears in The Times, nicknamed The Thunderer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is a nickname for The Times newspaper; the letters run across the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eth is an Old English letter, so it is an ancient written symbol.

clue.text: Chocolate biscuit: pound and fourteen shillings, in the old days?

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen

parts.words: fourteen shillings, in the old days
parts.note: a guinea was twenty-one shillings, so fourteen shillings is two-thirds of it: the first four of the word's six letters

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a chocolate biscuit would have cost in pre-decimal money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money alongside 'shillings', but it is an animal enclosure. The guinea is an old British coin worth 21 shillings; two-thirds of the word guinea gives two-thirds of its value.
explanation.definitionFit: A Penguin is a well-known British chocolate-covered biscuit bar.

clue.text: More than ten characters who look alike

definitions.meaning: a number from ten upwards is said to reach this
lookalike people, doubles, are figures in a scene

explanation.definitionFit: A score into two digits is above nine, and doubles are figures who resemble someone exactly.

clue.text: Political subversive, one infiltrating meeting to support measure

indicators.note: in a down clue the support sits below, so this piece comes after the measure

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width

indicators.note: the numeral gets inside the rendezvous, so this word signals a container

parts.note: a tryst is a lovers' meeting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A political agitator sneaks into a gathering in order to back some policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' works because in a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An entryist joins a party to subvert it from within, a type of political subversive.

clue.text: Believe councillor has to make changes

parts.note: to edit is to make changes to a text

explanation.surface: A local councillor accepts that changes must be made.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to accept it as true, a synonym for believe.

clue.text: Close friend, lively person for a the most part

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a spark is a lively, witty person

explanation.surface: A close pal is described as a lively sort, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the K from SPARK; the stray 'a' is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Spar is an informal word, chiefly Irish, for a mate or close pal.

clue.text: Mole keeps on meeting spy chief, the man who's in charge

indicators.note: the breakwater holds the other pieces inside it, so this word signals a container

parts.note: a mole is a harbour breakwater, a kind of pier
RE means on or concerning
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A double agent keeps a meeting with the spymaster who runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' wants to be a spy beside 'spy chief'; it is a harbour breakwater. 'meeting' just joins the two inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The premier is the prime minister, the person who leads a government.

clue.text: Newly-arrived undergraduates, first two to register initially, have time for drink

indicators.note: this pair comes at the start, ahead of the students
only the opening pair of letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: freshmen are first-year students

explanation.surface: New students, the first pair to sign up, have a moment for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshment covers food and drink taken to restore energy, so a drink is one.

clue.text: Member of religious group entering church in Dublin

indicators.note: the answer goes into the letters of these words, so this word signals a hidden run

explanation.surface: A believer from another faith walks into a Dublin church.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, one member of a religious community.

clue.text: Actor felt eye hurt, terrible pain in this sort of drama?

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An actor with an injured eye endures agony on stage, in a fitting type of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges ACTOR FELT EYE HURT into the answer's sixteen letters; the surface's pain fits the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Artaud's Theatre of Cruelty is a style of drama that assaults the audience's senses.

clue.text: Member of workers' group, possibly tiniest around

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A labour activist, perhaps the smallest one present.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade unionist belongs to a trade union, an organisation of workers.

clue.text: See 10
Beset by ailment, mother managed to survive the experience

indicators.note: the rearranged parent is surrounded by the ailment, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: a cough is a minor ailment

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Laid low by illness, a mother still got through the ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' gives METHRO, the anagram of the parent; it looks like the past tense of cope, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To come through is to survive or get through an ordeal unharmed.

clue.text: Assume I'm getting home in time

indicators.note: the at-home word goes within the period, so this word signals a container

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
IN means at home

explanation.surface: Someone supposes they will be back at the house on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' as IN (at home) is a standard crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to suppose or assume something is so.

clue.text: Pre-election promises finally abandoned, it's clear

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a manifesto sets out a party's pledges before an election

explanation.surface: Campaign pledges get dropped in the end, as is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means obvious or plain to see.

clue.text: Hotel close to centre: a warm, welcoming place

indicators.note: the hotel letter is set right next to the centre, after it

parts.note: the heart is the centre of something
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel near the town centre is described as warm and inviting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like part of a location phrase; it puts H right after HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside floor is the warm focal point of a home.

clue.text: Country agents trapping American fellow

indicators.note: the agency holds the other pieces inside it, so this word signals a container

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a bod is a person, a fellow

explanation.surface: Spies from one country seize a US citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: BOD is British slang for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: A journey, primarily to British island

indicators.note: this pair comes first, ahead of the journey

parts.note: a go can be a trip or turn, a journey

explanation.surface: Someone sets out on a trip, heading first for a British island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' places TO B ahead of A GO, although the clue gives them second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, part of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Guy on board boat's navigated into unoccupied bay

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the emptied bay, so this word signals a container
emptied of its middle, so only the outside letters of the word are used
the boat's letters are steered around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man on deck steers his vessel into a deserted bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navigated' gives OBSTA, the anagram of the boat's letters; 'unoccupied' empties bay to its first and last letters. 'Guy' is a rope, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobstay is a rope or chain holding the bowsprit down, a guy aboard ship.

clue.text: Welsh woman, busy sort who aspires to be different?

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name
a bee is proverbially busy

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman is a busy type who longs to be someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe longs to become someone they admire, usually spelt with one final E.

clue.text: Plant with nasty smell began to wither

parts.note: BO is body odour

indicators.note: withering twists the shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant giving off a foul stink started to droop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wither' gives GBEAN, the anagram of began; 'nasty smell' as BO (body odour) is standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogbean is a marsh plant, also called buckbean.

clue.text: Warning about area patrolled by old soldier

parts.note: CA (circa) means about

indicators.note: the old soldier surrounds the area letter, so this phrase signals a container

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, an old soldier

explanation.surface: A notice warns of a zone guarded by a former soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patrolled by' looks like a soldier walking a beat; it signals the area letter sitting inside the veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso, a type of warning.

clue.text: Female cleric accepting award Z with thanks

indicators.note: the cleric takes the award inside, so this word signals a container

parts.note: RR is short for Right Reverend, a title of a bishop
the OBE is a British honour
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A woman priest receives an honour and says thank you.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour; the stray Z in the held clue is an OCR artefact and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberta is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Given dope, as one born to be boy racer was?

definitions.meaning: dope is slang for information, so this means briefed on the latest

definitions.text: as one born to be boy racer was?
definitions.meaning: reared, from birth, with a taste for driving fast

explanation.definitionFit: Being briefed means getting the latest information, while a born speed fiend was raised for fast driving.

clue.text: See 23
Perfect newspaper costing 20p — a bargain

parts.note: the i was the Independent's cut-price sister paper, launched at 20p
a deal is a bargain

explanation.surface: A cheap newspaper is a perfect bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily newspaper launched by the Independent at 20p.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means perfect or the best possible.

clue.text: Boy not born in France, say

indicators.note: the born letter is left out of the country word

parts.note: France is one example of a country or land
N stands for born, from the Latin natus

explanation.surface: A boy who was not born in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France, say' looks like a place of birth; it gives LAND, from which 'not' removes N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a young male, a synonym for boy.

clue.text: Greeting sounds more shrill

indicators.note: the answer is pronounced like the pitch word, so this signals a homophone

parts.note: a shriller voice is higher in pitch

explanation.surface: A greeting is uttered at a more piercing pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiya is an informal hello.

clue.text: Wretched artist's dire need, suffering financial hardship

indicators.note: something wretched is in a bad way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter
a dire need is still a need: the adjective only intensifies, and the plain word joins the fodder

explanation.surface: A poor painter's desperate want, living in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wretched' signals the anagram of ARTIST and NEED; 'dire' only colours the surface, describing how bad the want is.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitened circumstances are those of poverty, too little money to live comfortably.
